title: Text processing with sed, tr and awk

sed-s.text: Show `~/dokument/server.log` with the word `ERROR` replaced by `FEL` on every line, using `sed`.

sed-d.text: Show server.log **without** all the lines containing `INFO`, using `sed`.
sed-d.hint: The address `/INFO/` selects the lines and the command `d` deletes them: `sed '/INFO/d' file`

tr-upper.text: Print every user name in `/etc/passwd` in **uppercase**: pick out field 1 with `cut` and pass it on to `tr`.
tr-upper.hint: `cut -d: -f1 /etc/passwd` gives you the user names. Add `| tr a-z A-Z`.

tr-path.text: Show the directories in `$PATH` on **separate lines** by replacing `:` with a newline using `tr`.

awk-print.text: Print the user name and shell (fields 1 and 7) from `/etc/passwd` with `awk`.
awk-print.hint: The fields are separated by colons, so use `-F:`. The program is `'{print $1, $7}'`.

awk-sum.text: Work out the **sum** of the points (column 3) in `~/dokument/betyg.csv` with `awk`.
awk-sum.hint: Skip the header line with `NR > 1`, add up with `summa += $3` and print the result in `END { }`. The separator is a comma: `-F,`.

sed-i.hint: Use `sed -i`. Since the replacement contains a `/`, it's easiest to switch delimiter: `s|Linux|GNU/Linux|`.
